newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bomber McVeigh seeks new trial.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bomber McVeigh seeks new trial.

text.p: Attorneys for Timothy McVeigh, who was convicted last month of the Oklahoma City bombing and sentenced to death, asked on Monday for a new trial.
"Mr McVeigh's life is literally at stake," attorney Robert Nigh told reporters after filing the 180-page request. He said the request sought a lesser sentence.

McVeigh was convicted on June 2 of bombing the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City on April 19, 1995, an attack that killed 168 people. On June 13, the same jury sentenced the Gulf War veteran to death.
In seeking a new trial, McVeigh's lawyers cited overwhelming prejudicial pre-trial publicity and victim impact testimony which the attorneys said was unfair to their client.

"It triggered a decision that was not based upon reason, but instead a decision that was based upon emotion," Nigh said, referring to the often heart-wrenching testimony given by victims and relatives of people who died in the bombing.
Nigh said the request for a new trial was based on 15 grounds, many of them technical legal issues.
